1.note: Isaiah is using the adjective **righteous** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [The righteous person perishes]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **covenant faithfulness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and the men who are faithful to the covenant]

The expression **are assembled** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [gather together]

Isaiah is using **from the face of** as a common expression of the culture to mean “because of.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [because of evil]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **evil**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [from evil actions]

Isaiah is using **setting it on the heart** as a common expression of the culture to mean “thinking carefully about it.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [taking it to heart] or [thinking carefully about it]

Isaiah is referring to the death of a righteous person in a polite way by using the phrase **the righteous is assembled**. Depending on what is helpful for your readers, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [God gathers the righteous to himself]

Isaiah is using the adjective **righteous** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [The one who acts rightly]

2.note: The pronoun **He** refers to the righteous person of whom Isaiah spoke in the previous verse. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [The righteous person enters peace]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **peace**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [He enters into a peaceful state]

Isaiah is referring to being dead and buried in a polite way by using the phrase **they rest on their beds**. Depending on what is helpful for your readers, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [the righteous people lie peacefully in death]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **uprightness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [as an upright person]

3.note: Isaiah uses the word **But you** here to indicate a contrast between the righteous people who died in peace and the sons of a sorceress who are being addressed. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [But as for you]

The word **you** and the implied “you” in the imperative **come near** are plural. The words “you” and “yourselves” are also plural in verses 4 and 5. So use plural forms in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

Yahweh is using **sons of a sorceress** as a common expression of the culture to mean people who are characterized by practicing sorcery, as if a sorceress were their mother. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [you people who practice sorcery]

Yahweh is using **seed of an adulterer** as a common expression of the culture to mean people who are characterized by unfaithfulness, as if an adulterer were their father. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [you unfaithful people]

4.note: Yahweh is using the question form to rebuke the people for mocking him. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [It is against me that you delight yourselves!]

Yahweh is using the question form to rebuke the people for insulting him. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation.

Opening the mouth wide and sticking out the tongue were symbolic actions by which people showed scorn and mockery toward someone. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [do you open the mouth wide and stick out the tongue to mock]

4.q: הֲ⁠לֽוֹא אַתֶּ֥ם יִלְדֵי פֶ֖שַׁע זֶ֥רַע שָֽׁקֶר
4.note: Yahweh is using the question form to emphasize that the people are rebellious and deceitful offspring. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [You certainly are children of transgression, seed of falsehood]

Yahweh is using **children of transgression** as a common expression of the culture to mean people who are characterized by rebellion. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [people who rebel]

Yahweh is using **seed of falsehood** as a common expression of the culture to mean people who are characterized by deceit. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [people who deceive others]

5.note: Yahweh is referring to immoral acts of pagan worship in a polite way by using the phrase **inflaming yourselves**. Depending on what is helpful for your readers, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [ones engaging in immoral worship among the oaks]

The expression **inflaming yourselves** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [ones who burn with lust among the oaks]

6.note: Yahweh actually means to communicate the opposite of the literal meaning of what he is saying here. He calls the smooth stones of the stream bed the people’s portion to show that, by choosing idols, they have rejected the true inheritance he offers. If a speaker of your language would not do that, you could translate the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [You would rather worship smooth stones than the living God]

Yahweh is using the adjective **smooth** as a noun to mean a certain kind of stone. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [Among the smooth stones of]

The words **you** and **your** are feminine singular because they refer to the nation of Israel personified as a woman. The words “you,” “your,” and “yourself” are feminine singular for the same reason in verses 7–13. So use singular forms in your translation if your language marks that distinction, and use feminine forms if your language marks that distinction.

The repeated pronoun **they** refers to the smooth stones of the streambed that the people worship as their gods. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [these, the smooth stones, are your lot]

Yahweh is using the question form to declare that he will not relent concerning these things. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [I will not relent over these things!]

7.note: Yahweh is referring to immoral acts of pagan worship in a polite way by using the phrase **You set your bed**. Depending on what is helpful for your readers, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [You commit sexual immorality]

Isaiah is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [to offer a sacrifice]

8.note: Yahweh is referring to acting unfaithfully like a prostitute in a polite way by using the phrase **you uncover {yourself}**. Depending on what is helpful for your readers, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [you expose yourself]

Yahweh is referring to pursuing many pagan lovers in a polite way by using the phrase **you make wide your bed**. Depending on what is helpful for your readers, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [you made room for them]

Yahweh is referring to intimate relations with those who worship idols in a polite way by using the phrase **You love their bed**. Depending on what is helpful for your readers, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [You lust after them] or [You delight in sexual orgies with them]

Yahweh is referring to a part of the male body in a polite way by using the phrase **you see a hand**. Depending on what is helpful for your readers, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [you gaze at their genitals]

9.note: Yahweh is speaking of the people’s worship of idols as if they were bringing gifts of **oil** and **perfumes**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And you come to Molech with oil, and you put on many perfumes to worship idols]
The word **you** is singular here because Yahweh is addressing the people of Israel as a single entity. So use the singular form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

9.q: וַ⁠תְּשַׁלְּחִ֤י צִרַ֨יִ⁠ךְ֙ עַד מֵ֣⁠רָחֹ֔ק וַ⁠תַּשְׁפִּ֖ילִי עַד שְׁאֽוֹל
9.note: Yahweh is referring to the extreme lengths the people go to in seeking help from other gods by naming two extremes, **faraway** and **Sheol**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [And you go to any length to seek other gods, even sending your envoys to distant lands and descending to the realm of the dead]

10.note: Yahweh is using **In the greatness of your way** as a common expression of the culture to mean “through your extensive travels.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [After going to such great lengths] or [In doing so very many things]

Yahweh is using **the life of your hand** as a common expression of the culture to mean “renewed strength.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [You find renewed strength]

11.note: Yahweh is using the question form to rebuke the people for fearing other gods more than they fear him. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [You must dread and fear someone else so much]

The terms **dread** and **fear** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [do you so greatly fear]

11.q: וְ⁠אוֹתִ⁠י֙ לֹ֣א זָכַ֔רְתְּ לֹא שַׂ֖מְתְּ עַל לִבֵּ֑⁠ךְ
11.note: Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and do not remember me, you do not set your heart on me] or [and do not remember me, you do not give me a thought]

11.q: הֲ⁠לֹ֨א אֲנִ֤י מַחְשֶׁה֙ וּ⁠מֵ֣⁠עֹלָ֔ם וְ⁠אוֹתִ֖⁠י לֹ֥א תִירָֽאִי
11.note: Yahweh is using the question form to assert that his long silence is the reason the people no longer fear him. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [It is me being silent even from eternity that you do not fear me.] or [It is because I have been silent from eternity that you do not fear me.]

Yahweh is speaking of withholding his judgment as if it were **being silent**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [me withholding my judgment]

12.note: This is poetic language. If your language has a way to indicate poetry, you could use it here. Isaiah repeats **I** for emphasis before saying what he **will declare**. Alternate translation: [As for me, I will declare your righteousness and your deeds]

Yahweh actually means to communicate the opposite of the literal meaning of what he is saying here, meaning that he will reveal the truth about them. If a speaker of your language would not do that, you could translate the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the true nature of your character and actions]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **righteousness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [how righteous you are]

Isaiah is emphasizing a positive meaning by using a negative word, **not**, together with a mild expression, **benefit**, that is the opposite of the intended meaning. If it would be helpful in your language, you could emphasize the positive meaning in a strong way. Alternate translation: [and they will certainly condemn you]

13.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **collection**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the idols you have gathered]

13.q: וְ⁠אֶת כֻּלָּ֥⁠ם יִשָּׂא ר֖וּחַ יִקַּח הָ֑בֶל
13.note: Yahweh is speaking of how powerless the idols are as if they were objects so light that **the wind will carry all of them away** and **a breath will take** them. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [But your idols are so powerless that a gentle breeze could blow them away]

The implication is that **the mountain of my holiness** refers to Mount Zion in Jerusalem, where Yahweh’s temple was located. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Mount Zion in Jerusalem, where my temple is located]

Yahweh is speaking of people trusting him for protection as if they were **taking refuge in** him. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [But the one trusting me for protection]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **holiness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [my holy mountain]

14.note: Here the author is using the pronoun **one** in a general sense, not to refer to specific people. Use an expression for this that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [And a person will say]
This is the beginning of what an unspecified person will say. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could mark that this is a direct quote.

The implied “you” in these imperatives is plural. (The addressees are not named, but the context suggests that they are the other nations that have kept the Israelites captive and must now free and return them.) So use plural forms in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

14.q: פַּנּוּ דָ֑רֶךְ הָרִ֥ימוּ מִכְשׁ֖וֹל מִ⁠דֶּ֥רֶךְ עַמִּֽ⁠י
14.note: Yahweh is speaking of removing everything that hinders his people from returning to him as if it were building a road and lifting a stumbling block from it. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Clear the path! Remove everything that hinders my people from returning to me]

15.note: The adjectives **high** and **uplifted** mean similar things. Isaiah is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [the supremely exalted one]
Here, **his name** represents Yahweh himself. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and he is holy]

Yahweh is speaking of people who are humble and repentant as if they had been **crushed**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the contrite and the humble in spirit]

Yahweh is using the adjectives **crushed** and **lowly** as nouns to mean certain kinds of people. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate these adjectives with equivalent phrases. Alternate translation: [people who are crushed and people who are humble in spirit]

15.q: לְ⁠הַחֲיוֹת֙ ר֣וּחַ שְׁפָלִ֔ים וּֽ⁠לְ⁠הַחֲי֖וֹת לֵ֥ב נִדְכָּאִֽים
15.note: These two clauses mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [to revive those who are lowly and crushed]

16.note: The word translated as **For** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [This is because]

Here, **my face** represents Yahweh’s presence. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [from before me] or [from being in my presence]

Here, **the breaths** represents the living people whom Yahweh has made. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and the living people that I myself have made]

17.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **iniquity**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [For how wickedly he acted to gain wealth]
The pronoun **him** refers to the people of Israel. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and I struck them]

Yahweh is describing one event, **I hid**, before describing another event that preceded it, **I was angry**. If it would be helpful your language, you may wish to relate these events in the order in which they happened. Alternate translation: [I was angry, so I hid]

Yahweh is using **I hid** as a common expression of the culture to mean “I withdrew my favor from the people.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I withdrew my favor]

Yahweh is speaking of the people (in the singular) persisting in their own rebellious desires as if a person **went backward in the way of his heart**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [but he kept following his own rebellious desires]

18.note: Yahweh uses the word **and** here to indicate a contrast between the people’s sinful ways and his decision to heal and restore them. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [I have seen his ways. Nevertheless, I will heal him]

Yahweh is speaking of restoring the people to well-being as if he would **heal** a sick person. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and I will restore him to well-being]

19.note: Here, **the lips** represents what a person says, in this case words of praise. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the praise that people speak]

Yahweh is repeating the word **peace** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [Complete peace]

Yahweh is referring to all people by naming two extremes, **the faraway** and **the near**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [to everyone everywhere]

20.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **the driven sea** cannot rest and keeps churning up mud, so **the wicked** find no peace and continually produce evil. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [But the wicked will find no peace, just as the driven sea keeps churning]

Yahweh is using the plural adjective **wicked** as a noun to mean people of a certain kind. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase, here and in the next verse. Alternate translation: [But wicked people]

21.note: Here Isaiah marks these words as a direct quotation of what Yahweh says. If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this as an indirect quotation. Alternate translation: [My God says that there is no peace for the wicked]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **peace**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [Nothing will be well]
